provenance.note: Generated by drivers/survival on the pystatsval harness against a PyPI-installed pystatistics==4.2.0. 4.2.0 is the optimization+robustness release on top of 4.0.0/4.1.0: Cox PH was rewritten from O(n^2) to O(n log n) (results bit-for-bit unchanged), the coefficient models gained .conf_int / conf_level (4.1.0), and the GPU GLM backend stopped falsely rejecting correct float32 fits (so discrete_time on GPU is now reliable). Correctness fits both pystatistics and R survival on the identical survival::lung rows; discrete-time is validated against R glm(binomial) on the identical reconstructed person-period design. The Cox PH scaling study sweeps a synthetic proportional-hazards DGP on CPU. Host: powerhouse (Apple Silicon, CPU fp64, R 4.5.2 / survival 3.8.3).
provenance.baseline: Compare against reports/survival-v4.0.0.md (the pre-optimization baseline). Correctness is unchanged at 4.2.0; the optimization changed Cox PH from O(n^2) to O(n log n) (the scaling study's pystatistics/R ratio went from growing 23x->812x to flat ~1-2.6x), and the consistency findings O1/O2/C2/C3 from the 4.0.0 report are now resolved.

r.engine: R survival::survfit / survdiff / coxph; glm(binomial) for discrete-time

reference.name: R survival::survfit / survdiff / coxph
reference.what: The R survival package (Therneau): survfit() for Kaplan-Meier, survdiff() for the log-rank test, coxph() for proportional hazards. Discrete-time survival is validated against R glm(family=binomial) on the identical person-period design pystatistics builds internally.

studies.title: Correctness vs R survival — Powerhouse (CPU / fp64), per quantity
Wall-clock vs R on survival::lung — Powerhouse (CPU / fp64)
studies.note: Per-fit median over timed repeats. With the 4.2.0 O(n log n) Cox PH, all four procedures are now within a small constant factor of R on the tiny lung dataset; the scaling study below carries the asymptotic claim.

studies.title: Cox PH CPU scaling vs R — Powerhouse (CPU / fp64)
studies.note: Synthetic proportional-hazards DGP. With the 4.2.0 rewrite, pystatistics Cox PH is O(n log n) (vectorized reverse-cumsum risk sets + a Fenwick-tree concordance), matching R's complexity: the pystatistics/R wall ratio is now FLAT at ~1-2.6x across n=250..8000 (it grew 23x->812x in v4.0.0, the O(n^2)-vs-O(n log n) signature). Results are bit-for-bit unchanged. True O(n) is impossible for Cox (the event-time sort is O(n log n)); R is O(n log n) too, and we match it.

record_fields.max_abs: max absolute difference between pystatistics and R over a quantity's elements
record_fields.max_rel: max relative difference between pystatistics and R over a quantity's elements (correctness headline)
record_fields.n_elements: number of scalar elements compared for that quantity (1 for scalars, vector length otherwise)
record_fields.speedup_vs_r: R wall-clock / pystatistics wall-clock on the same fit (>1 means pystatistics is faster)
record_fields.ratio_pystat_over_r: pystatistics wall-clock / R wall-clock at a given n (flat across n once both are O(n log n))
